payload.title: Editing LiPD Files
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook demonstrates how to edit LiPD files using the PyLiPD library. It covers modifying existing properties, adding new metadata, and creating ensemble tables within a LiPD-formatted dataset. The notebook utilizes object-oriented programming techniques to manipulate dataset properties and save the edited dataset to a new file. The process involves generating unique identifiers, editing geographical coordinates, adding publication information, and creating ensemble tables for paleoclimate studies.
goals: Add information in a new object (e.g., publication information)
Save the edited dataset to a new file

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduces the purpose of the notebook, which is to edit LiPD files by changing existing information, adding new metadata, and creating ensemble tables.
section_blurbs.heading: Editing LiPD Files

section_blurbs.blurb: Demonstrates how to correct errors in existing properties, such as geographical coordinates, using the PyLiPD library.
section_blurbs.heading: Editing an exisiting property

section_blurbs.blurb: Explains how to add new properties to a dataset, focusing on identifying and tagging variables related to temperature analysis.
section_blurbs.heading: Creating new properties

section_blurbs.blurb: Shows how to add publication information to a dataset by creating and populating Publication objects with details like title, authors, and journal.
section_blurbs.heading: Adding new information from classes

section_blurbs.blurb: Describes the process of generating ensemble tables for age models using Bayesian methods and integrating them into the dataset.
section_blurbs.heading: Adding an Ensemble Table

section_blurbs.blurb: Covers the final step of saving the edited dataset back into a LiPD file format using the PyLiPD library.
section_blurbs.heading: Writing to a LiPD file

section_blurbs.blurb: Lists references for further reading on Bayesian age modeling and other related topics.
section_blurbs.heading: References
